subject.title: [Feature]: Fallback approval mode + model attribution in messages

question: Should OpenClaw add a core per-agent approval gate before executing configured model fallbacks, or should fallback remain automatic with visibility handled through prefixes/logs/status surfaces?
rationale: The missing behavior requires a new fallback/config contract in a compatibility-sensitive provider path; code inspection shows no existing narrow hook that can be safely wired without choosing UX, timeout, and reliability semantics.

options.title: Add per-agent opt-in approval
options.body: Introduce a default-off per-agent fallback approval policy with explicit timeout and fail/proceed behavior, then update schema, docs, runtime fallback tests, and channel proof.

options.title: Keep fallback automatic
options.body: Close or narrow this issue after documenting that attribution/logging/status are the supported transparency surfaces and fallback confirmation should live outside core orchestration.

options.title: Design approval seam first
options.body: Defer this specific gate until a broader approval resolver API can cover fallback, plugin, and tool-interrupt workflows consistently.

recommendation.title: Add per-agent opt-in approval
recommendation.body: Introduce a default-off per-agent fallback approval policy with explicit timeout and fail/proceed behavior, then update schema, docs, runtime fallback tests, and channel proof.
